definitions.explanation: Behavior characterized by doing what one wants without considering others; selfishness or capriciousness.

examples.japanese: わがままを{言|い}わないで。
examples.english: Don't be selfish. / Don't make selfish demands.
examples.notes: わがままを言う = to make selfish demands

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はわがままな{子|こ}だ。
わがままを{許|ゆる}してください。
examples.notes: Often used apologetically when making a personal request

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}はわがままで、いつも{自分|じぶん}の{思|おも}い{通|どお}りにしたがる。
examples.english: That person is selfish and always wants things to go their own way.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のわがままを{何|なん}でも{聞|き}いていると、{大人|おとな}になってから{困|こま}ることになる。
examples.english: If you give in to every selfish demand a child makes, it will cause problems when they grow up.
examples.notes: わがままを{聞|き}く = to give in to selfish demands

notes:
USAGE: わがまま describes selfish or willful behavior, often used for children who won't listen or adults who prioritize their own desires. Can be written {我儘|わがまま} in kanji.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・わがままを{言|い}う (to make selfish demands)
・わがままな{人|ひと} (a selfish person)
・わがままを{通|とお}す (to have one's own way)

REGISTER: Can be used critically or self-deprecatingly. When used about oneself, it can be a humble way to apologize for a request.
